rationale: C17 is the strongest plausible template because it establishes the precise Mutual Security Act administrative framework used by the child, expressly reserves the President's section 502(c) function, delegates the surrounding functions to the Director for Mutual Security, and defines “functions” to include duties, powers, responsibilities, authority, and discretion. The child then performs that reserved section 502(c) function using closely corresponding terminology and an exception-based enumeration of powers that will not continue. C19 offers a weaker structural analogue involving identification of powers to continue or allow to lapse, while C16 supplies the general form of a Mutual Security Act determination-and-notification letter but not the child's distinctive machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: all of the powers, functions, and responsibilities transferred to the Director for Mutual Security by subsection (b)(2) of section 502 of said act are necessary
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The functions conferred upon the President by sections 502(c), 503, 507, and 530 of the said Mutual Security Act of 1951
shared_material.explanation: The parent expressly isolates section 502(c) as a presidential function; the child is the later instrument exercising that reserved function.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Powers, functions, and responsibilities under the Economic Cooperation Act of 1948, as amended, with respect to the following are not necessary
shared_material.parent_excerpt: There are hereby excluded from the functions delegated by section 1(a) of this order
shared_material.explanation: Both use an exception-based administrative structure: a broad body of functions is addressed first, followed by a specific enumeration of excluded or noncontinuing functions.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the basic powers of the Economic Cooperation Act, appropriately redirected toward the new objectives, are necessary to enable the Director for Mutual Security
shared_material.parent_excerpt: references in prior Executive orders to the Economic Cooperation Administration [and] the Administrator for Economic Cooperation ... are amended to refer to the Mutual Security Agency [and] the Director for Mutual Security
shared_material.explanation: The child applies the parent’s machinery for carrying former Economic Cooperation functions forward under the new Mutual Security Agency and Director.
